source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Islamic Religious Education, Grade 5 (Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly from 'grade 5 designs/GRADE-5-IRE-Curriculum-Designs.pdf' via the Read tool (no pages param), full text, all 7 strands / 24 numbered sub-strand headings (29 taught topics once 1.1's 4 named surah, 3.3.2's 3 named prophet miracles, and 4.2's split Qabliyah/Ba'diyah + Taraweeh/Witr experiences are counted per the same one-skill-per-named-item precedent Grade 6/7 IRE used) / 90 lessons. Learning Area allocation: 3 lessons/week at Upper Primary (Religious Education line).

subStrands.name: 1.1 Selected Surah
subStrands.notes: The design names 4 specific surahs under this one sub-strand heading, no further breakdown given: Al-Kauthar, Al-Maun, Al-Quraysh, Al-Fil. Following the Grade 6/7 IRE precedent (splitting a single 'Selected Surah' sub-strand into one skill per named surah), this sub-strand is implemented as 4 skills, one per surah.
specificLearningOutcomes: read the selected surahs for spiritual nourishment
recite the selected surahs for devotional activities
outline the basic meaning of the selected surahs
deduce lessons from the selected surah
appreciate the Qur'an as the first source of guidance
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to recite the Qur'an?
What lessons do we learn from the selected surahs?
learningExperiences: listen to the teacher/resource person/digital device on the recitation of the selected surah
recite the selected surahs after the teacher/peer/or from a digital device
read the selected surahs from a digital device/mus-haf/charts
practise pronunciation through listening to digital devices
recite the selected surahs severally to enhance memorisation
listen to the basic meaning of the selected surahs from digital devices and make notes
discuss the different ways of applying the teachings and lessons learnt from the selected surahs
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening enhanced through group discussion on ways of applying the teachings of the selected surahs
Digital literacy: interacting with technology as learners listen to the basic meaning of the selected surahs from digital devices and write notes
linkedLearningAreas: English — learners relate the reading skills used in English and Arabic to read the surah
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric rewards reading, reciting AND explaining the meaning of ALL verses of the selected surah, plus deducing and applying lessons in life at the top band — recitation accuracy and applied meaning are both explicitly assessed, not meaning alone.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Hadith on Good Behaviour
specificLearningOutcomes: identify examples of good behaviour from the selected Hadith for character building
discuss the significance of the selected Hadith in shaping the character of a Muslim
apply good behaviour in day-to-day life
appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by applying them in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should one behave well?
What actions show that you fear Allah?
learningExperiences: read from chart/digital devices the Hadith on good behaviour: "Fear Allah wherever you are and follow up a bad deed with a good deed, it will wipe it out. And behave well towards other people." (Al-Tirmidhi)
identify good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith and present in plenary
discuss the teachings and relevance of the Hadith in their daily life
role-play acts showing good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening and teamwork as learners discuss the teachings and relevance of the Hadith in daily life
Learning to learn: sharing learnt knowledge as learners identify good behaviour mentioned in the Hadith
linkedLearningAreas: Languages: Arabic and English as they read and explain the meaning of the Hadith

subStrands.name: 2.2 Hadith on Greetings
specificLearningOutcomes: assess the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim
practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity in the society
appreciate the use of Islamic greetings in bringing harmony in the society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim use Islamic greeting?
learningExperiences: read the Hadith on greetings: "Shall I inform you of something which, if you do, you will love one another? Promote greetings (salaam) amongst yourselves." (Muslim)
watch/listen to Islamic greetings from digital devices
demonstrate Islamic greetings, in pairs
discuss the importance of Islamic greetings in the life of a Muslim and make summary notes
search online and sing Qasida on Islamic greetings
practise Islamic greetings to promote love and unity as learners come to class/school
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: teamwork through group discussion on the importance of Islamic greetings
Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learners search online to access Qasida on Islamic greetings
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — as learners listen and sing Qasida on Islamic greetings

subStrands.name: 2.3 Hadith on Knowledge
specificLearningOutcomes: read the Hadith as a source of reference in seeking knowledge
assess the importance of seeking knowledge for the benefit of this world and the Hereafter
appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by working hard in school
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to seek knowledge in Islam?
What challenges may hinder one from acquiring education?
learningExperiences: read from a chart/digital devices the Hadith on knowledge: "Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim." (Al-Tirmidhi)
search online the importance of seeking knowledge and present it in class
discuss ways of improving academic performance in school
role-play acts on the importance of seeking knowledge in the Muslim society
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: interpretation and inference as learners proactively discuss ways of improving academic performance in their school
Digital literacy: interacting with digital literacy as learners search online for information on the importance of seeking knowledge
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners role-play acts on the importance of seeking knowledge in the Muslim society
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — aspects of rights to education

subStrands.name: 2.4 Hadith on Gratitude
specificLearningOutcomes: read the Hadith on gratitude for character formation
practise gratitude in day-to-day life
appreciate the teachings of the Hadith by exercising gratitude
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should one be grateful to other people?
learningExperiences: read from a chart/digital device the Hadith on gratitude: "Whoever is never thankful to people is never thankful to Allah." (Al-Tirmithi)
discuss the lessons learnt from the Hadith and make class presentations
dramatise ways that show gratitude
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the lessons learnt from the Hadith
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners dramatise ways that show gratitude
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the aspect of gratitude in life skills
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (2.0 Hadith) rubric rewards reading AND explaining the teachings, plus deducing and applying lessons in daily life at the top band — recall of the Hadith text alone is not sufficient for top marks.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Belief in Allah — Attributes of Allah
subStrands.notes: 6 named attributes: Al-Ghaffaar (The Forgiver), Al-Alim (The All Knowing), Al-Hafeedh (The Protector), Al-Hakam (The Judge), Al-Hayu (The Ever Living), Al-Waahid (The One).
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the attributes of Allah and their corresponding meaning
assess the importance of the attributes of Allah
use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplication)
appreciate the unique attributes of Allah as part of Islamic faith
keyInquiryQuestions: What lessons are learnt from the attributes of Allah?
Why should one use the attributes of Allah while making dua (supplications)?
learningExperiences: listen to the recitation of the attributes of Allah from a digital device
match the attributes of Allah with corresponding meaning using flash cards
discuss the importance of the attributes of Allah and make notes
use the attributes of Allah while making dua
sing qasida on the attributes of Allah
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination: networking as learners match the attributes of Allah with corresponding meaning using flash cards
Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the importance of the attributes of Allah
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — as learners sing qasida using attributes of Allah

subStrands.name: 3.2 Belief in Angels — Characteristics of Angels
specificLearningOutcomes: state the characteristics of angels to strengthen their iman
assess the significance of the belief in angels in the life of a Muslim
differentiate between angels and human beings to appreciate Allah's creation
appreciate the belief in angels as a pillar of iman
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the significance of believing in angels?
How can Muslims show obedience to Allah?
learningExperiences: search for information on the characteristics of angels from digital devices/books/resource persons and present in class
brainstorm on the significance of belief in angels and make notes
role-play different situations that depict obedience to Allah's commands (obeying parents, teachers, elders, school rules)
read a verse from the Qur'an on the obedience of angels on Allah's commands (Q66:6)
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork as learners brainstorm on the significance of belief in angels
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners role-play situations that depict obedience to Allah's commands
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — role-play of obedience to parents, teachers, elders, school rules

subStrands.name: 3.3.1 Belief in Prophets — Qualities of Prophets
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the qualities of prophets for character formation
apply values learnt from the qualities of prophets in their daily lives
appreciate belief in Allah's prophets by emulating the qualities of prophets
keyInquiryQuestions: How can qualities of the prophets be applied in daily life?
Why are prophets regarded as role models?
learningExperiences: search for information on the qualities of prophets from digital devices/books/resource persons and display in class
narrate a story of any prophet that shows these qualities
role-play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the prophets (e.g. honesty, obedience, patience)
discuss how the qualities of the prophets learnt can be applied in school situation
coreCompetencies: Self-efficacy: effective communication developed as learners narrate a story of any prophet that shows these qualities
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners role-play situations that demonstrate values learnt from the qualities of the prophets
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — values (honesty, obedience, patience) related to Life Skills

subStrands.name: 3.3.2 Miracles of Prophets
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith)
explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets
appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: What is a miracle?
Why did prophets perform miracles?
learningExperiences: match/listen to stories of the miracles of the selected prophets from digital devices and make notes
deduce lessons from the miracles of the selected prophets and present in class
match the name of the prophets with miracles performed using flash cards
draw, colour and display items related to the miracles of the selected prophet
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: creativity as learners match the name of the prophets with miracles performed using flash cards
Creativity and imagination: experimenting as learners draw, colour and display items related to the miracles of the selected prophet
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — as they draw and colour different items
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (3.0 Pillars of Iman) rubric top band requires outlining ALL 6 attributes of Allah with meaning AND mentioning all 6 pillars of Iman while explaining the significance of belief in angels exhaustively — a partial attribute list or shallow explanation caps below top band.

subStrands.name: 4.1 Nullifiers of Swalah
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the nullifiers of swalah to safeguard its validity
perform swalah correctly to earn thawab from Allah
differentiate between nullifiers of swalah and wudhu to perfect ibadah
appreciate performance of swalah by avoiding its nullifiers
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should one safeguard swalah?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the nullifiers of swalah and present in class
role-play some of the observable nullifiers of swalah (e.g. walking, eating, drinking, jumping)
match and sort the nullifiers of swalah and wudhu using flash cards
demonstrate the correct performance of swalah
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination: experimenting as learners role-play observable nullifiers of swalah (walking, eating, drinking, jumping)
Self-efficacy: effective communication as learners demonstrate the correct performance of swalah
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — observing and maintaining cleanliness

subStrands.name: 4.2 Sunnah (Optional) Prayers — Qabliyah and Ba'diyah
specificLearningOutcomes: assess the significance of performing sunnah prayers in the life of a Muslim
perform Qabliyah and Ba'diyah prayers to earn rewards from Allah
appreciate the performance of Qabliyah and Ba'diyah to emulate the sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.)
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim perform Qabliya and Ba'diyah?
learningExperiences: discuss sunnah prayers performed before and after fardh prayers and display in class using charts
match/fill gaps using digital devices/charts/pocket boards the number of raakat for Qabliyah and Ba'diyah for each fardh prayer
brainstorm on the importance of observing Qabliyah and Ba'diyah and write notes
perform Qabliyah and Ba'diyah prayers
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: interacting with technology as learners match/fill gaps using digital devices
Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss sunnah prayers
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — counting the number of Qabliya and Ba'diyah in each fardh prayer and their daily total, relating to addition

subStrands.name: 4.2.2 Taraweeh and Witr
specificLearningOutcomes: assess the significance of performing Taraweeh and witr prayers in the life of a Muslim
perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment
appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab
develop a habit of performing Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn blessing of Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the significance of performing swalatul Taraweeh and witr?
learningExperiences: watch a video on the performance of swalatul Taraweeh and witr through digital devices and discuss the procedure
demonstrate/role-play swalatul Taraweeh and witr in class
discuss the importance of performing swalatul Taraweeh and witr and present in class
keep personal logs for a week on how they perform Taraweeh/witr prayers
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the importance of performing swalatul Taraweeh and witr
Self-efficacy: executing a task as learners demonstrate/role-play swalatul Taraweeh and witr
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — relating to the concept of even and odd numbers (witr = odd-numbered raka'at)

subStrands.name: 4.3 Swadaqah (Charity)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify forms of swadaqah for character development
demonstrate different acts of swadaqah to earn rewards
assess the benefits of practising acts of swadaqah in society
appreciate the different forms of swadaqah in their daily life
keyInquiryQuestions: What acts of swadaqah do Muslims perform?
What are the benefits of practising swadaqah?
learningExperiences: get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class

discuss the different forms of swadaqah, in pairs/groups, as per the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w) (such as feeding an animal, removing an obstacle/harmful from the path/roads, sharing with others)
participate in charitable activities (clean-up exercise, visit to children's home, tree planting)
discuss the benefits of giving charity and make class presentation
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the benefits of giving charity
Learning to learn: working collaboratively as learners participate in charitable activities
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — getting pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and displaying them

subStrands.name: 4.4 Saum
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the conditions for saum as a requirement for its validity
apply the virtues acquired from observing saum in day-to-day life
appreciate observing saum as an act of ibadah
keyInquiryQuestions: What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?
What is the significance of fasting?
learningExperiences: discuss the conditions for saum and present in class
brainstorm on the virtues learnt from saum (patience, honesty, self-control, empathy, generosity) and display on charts
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: speaking, listening, writing and teamwork as learners brainstorm on the virtues learnt from saum (patience, honesty, self-control, empathy, generosity etc.)
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — discussing the benefits of fasting

subStrands.name: 4.4.1 Nullifiers of Saum (fasting)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the nullifiers of saum to safeguard the validity of saum
practise saum as a pillar of Islam
appreciate fasting as a means of gaining taqwa (piety)
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should Muslims observe rules and regulation when fasting?
What virtues do Muslims learn from fasting?
learningExperiences: discuss the nullifiers of saum and make presentation in class
sort nullifiers of saum from conditions of saum on flash cards
brainstorm on rules and regulations of saum and make class presentation
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: creativity as learners sort nullifiers of saum from conditions of saum on flash cards
Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the nullifiers of saum
linkedLearningAreas: Languages: Arabic and English — new vocabulary as learners discuss the nullifiers of saum
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (4.0 Devotional Acts) rubric top band requires performing Qabliyah, Ba'diyah, witr AND Taraweeh consistently, plus stating conditions of saum AND nullifiers of BOTH swalah and saum comprehensively — a skill covering only one prayer type or only one nullifier set (swalah OR saum, not both) misses part of the tested competency.

subStrands.name: 5.1 Virtues — Generosity
specificLearningOutcomes: assess the importance of practising generosity in the life of a Muslim
practise generosity as a virtue for character formation
appreciate the virtue of generosity as a means of earning rewards from Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim practise generosity?
When should a Muslim practise generosity?
learningExperiences: narrate short stories portraying generosity
watch/listen to a story on generosity and deduce the teachings
discuss the importance of observing generosity, and present in class
participate in activities that involve practising generosity
role-play activities that encourage generosity
coreCompetencies: Citizenship: enhanced as learners participate in activities that involve practising generosity
Self-efficacy: sharing learnt knowledge as learners narrate short stories portraying generosity
Creativity and innovation: networking as learners role-play activities that encourage generosity
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts — role-playing activities that encourage generosity

subStrands.name: 5.2 Effects of Social Media
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the positive and negative effects of social media on the youth
describe ways of using social media to facilitate learning
use social media responsibly to benefit self and others
keyInquiryQuestions: How can one use social media positively?
How can social media enhance learning?
learningExperiences: debate on the positive and negative effects of social media
discuss how to use social media responsibly and present in class
demonstrate how to use social media to facilitate learning using a digital device
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening and speaking as learners debate on the positive and negative effects of social media
Digital literacy: interacting with technology as learners demonstrate how to use social media to facilitate learning
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — content on social media

subStrands.name: 5.3 Prohibitions in Islam — Evils of Gambling
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the evils of gambling to promote responsible citizenship
describe ways of discouraging gambling in society
appreciate the prohibition of gambling by working hard for halaal (legal) earning
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the effects of participating in gambling?
Why is gambling forbidden in Islam?
learningExperiences: discuss the effects of gambling and present in class (loss of property, family breakdown)
role-play the effects of gambling
brainstorm on ways of discouraging gambling in society and display on a chart
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork as learners discuss the effects of gambling (loss of property, family breakdown)
Critical thinking and problem solving: decision making as learners brainstorm on ways of discouraging gambling in society
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the concept of resource management

subStrands.name: 5.4 Dua (Supplications) — Dua on Increase in Knowledge
subStrands.notes: Numbered '5.4' in the Summary of Strands and Sub-Strands table but '5.5' in the detailed strand body text — an apparent numbering inconsistency in the source PDF (same class of issue CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md flags to record verbatim, not silently resolve). Used '5.4' here to match the summary table's sequential position after 5.3.
specificLearningOutcomes: recite the selected dua to attain beneficial knowledge
assess the importance of the dua of seeking knowledge
apply the dua in day-to-day life
appreciate the act of supplication as a form of Ibadah (act of worship)
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the importance of reciting dua always?
learningExperiences: listen and recite the following dua from a digital device/teacher: "Oh Allah make what you teach me beneficial, teach me what is beneficial, and increase me in knowledge"
recite the dua every morning before start of class
brainstorm on the importance of reciting dua and write notes
coreCompetencies: Communication: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners brainstorm on the importance of making dua
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili — reading skills as they recite the dua
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (5.0 Akhlaq) rubric top band requires practising generosity AND using social media positively consistently, plus describing the evils of gambling correctly with cited examples — a skill covering only one of generosity/social-media, or gambling recall without concrete examples, misses part of the tested competency.

subStrands.name: 6.1 Etiquette of Islamic Wedding Celebrations
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the etiquette to be observed during Islamic wedding celebrations
outline unislamic activities that take place during wedding celebrations
appreciate Islamic wedding celebrations as part of Islamic heritage
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the Islamic etiquette that guides wedding celebrations?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended and note down what they observed/experienced
watch an Islamic wedding celebration from a digital device and the etiquette observed
sort the Islamic and unislamic activities performed during wedding celebrations using flash cards
role-play the etiquette to be observed during the wedding celebration (such as appropriate dressing, gender separation, avoiding Israaf and music)
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: as learners brainstorm on a wedding celebration they have attended
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners role-play the etiquette to be observed during the celebration
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — experiences encountered during wedding celebrations
scopeNotes: include: unislamic activities to sort against (dressing, gender separation, avoiding Israaf/extravagance and music) are named explicitly and are in scope as the contrast set for the Islamic-etiquette categorize content.

subStrands.name: 6.2 Rights of Neighbours
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the rights of neighbours for harmonious living
uphold the rights of neighbours as an act of ibadah
appreciate the rights of neighbours as an obligatory act upon a Muslim
keyInquiryQuestions: How should Muslims relate with neighbours?
What is the significance of upholding good neighbourliness?
learningExperiences: search the rights of neighbours in Islam using digital devices/print media and make notes
discuss the significance of treating neighbours well and display on a chart
dramatise the right way of treating neighbours
search for Hadith on the rights of neighbours and deduce lessons from it using digital devices/books/resource persons
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork as learners discuss the significance of treating neighbours well
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners dramatise the right way of treating neighbours
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — searching for the rights of neighbours

subStrands.name: 6.3 Islamic Rules on Buying and Selling
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the Islamic rules on buying and selling to promote a healthy business society
state the benefits of observing the Islamic rules on buying and selling
appreciate Islamic etiquette on the rules and regulations of buying and selling to earn rewards from Allah (Q83:1-6)
keyInquiryQuestions: What should Muslims avoid while buying and selling?
What are Islamic teachings on buying and selling?
learningExperiences: discuss Islamic rules on buying and selling and make oral presentation
discuss the benefits of observing Islamic rules and regulations on buying and selling
search Hadith on buying and selling and write notes on lessons learnt
role-play the Islamic rules and regulations on buying and selling
name commodities that they have bought from the market
undertake a project of creating a shop corner by collecting items, write a price list and a list of Islamic rules to be observed
coreCompetencies: Creativity and imagination: networking as learners undertake a project of creating a shop corner
Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and teamwork discussing the benefits of observing Islamic rules and regulations on buying and selling
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — creating a shop corner and buying/selling
scopeNotes: include: Q83:1-6 (Surah Al-Mutaffifin, on cheating in measure) is named as the scriptural basis — cited explicitly as the source for why fair dealing in buying/selling matters.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (6.0 Muamalat) rubric top band requires consistently demonstrating awareness of different relationships (wedding etiquette, neighbours, buying/selling) AND consistently applying Islamic teachings in interactions with others — recall of the rules alone, without an applied-scenario dimension, is only mid-band.

subStrands.name: 7.1 Al-Isra wal Miraj
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the Prophet's Night Journey to Heaven for spiritual nourishment
assess the significance of al-Isra wal Miraj in the life of a Muslim
appreciate al-Isra wal Miraj as an important event in the history of Islam
keyInquiryQuestions: What lessons do you learn from the Prophet's journey?
learningExperiences: watch a video on al-Isra wal Miraj from a digital device
discuss the events of al-Isra wal Miraj
discuss the importance of al-Isra wal Miraj
discuss the major gift given to Prophet (S.A.W) during al-Isra wal Miraj journey
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learners watch an audio-visual clip on al-Isra wal Miraj
Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking and writing as learners discuss the importance of al-Isra wal Miraj
Self-efficacy: effective communication as learners read reference material on the events and narrate it in class
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the means of transport used by the Prophet during the event
scopeNotes: include: the major gift given to the Prophet (S.A.W.) during the journey — the five daily prayers (swalah) — is an explicitly named learning experience, not just 'events happened.'

subStrands.name: 7.2 Pledges of Aqabah
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah
state the terms of the pledges of Aqabah
appreciate the pledges of Aqabah as a base for the migration of Muslims in Madina
keyInquiryQuestions: How did Muslims benefit from the pledges of Aqabah?
learningExperiences: discuss the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah and present in class
watch a video on the pledges of Aqaba from a digital device and write the terms
search for the terms of the pledges of Aqabah from books/digital device and note them down in their books
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: through discussions, in groups, on the events that led to the signing of the pledges of Aqabah
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the concept of signing agreements

subStrands.name: 7.3 Hijra to Madina
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the events on the Prophet's migration to Madina
assess the significance of the Prophet (S.A.W)'s journey to Madina
appreciate the Prophet (S.A.W.)'s journey to Madina as a milestone in Islamic History
keyInquiryQuestions: Why did the Prophet (S.A.W.) migrate to Madina?
Why is Hijra important to Muslims?
learningExperiences: listen/watch a story on the Prophet (S.A.W.)'s migration to Madina from a digital device/teacher
brainstorm reasons for Prophet's migration to Madina and write notes
discuss the major events that took place during the migration (e.g. the Prophet leaving Ali in his house, departure with Abubakar, at cave Thaur, the incident of Suraqah, reception in Madina)
sing a Qasida of welcoming the Prophet (S.A.W) i.e. Talaal Badru 'alaynaa
discuss the significance of Hijra and make short note (such as end of persecution, unity of the Ummah, beginning of the Islamic calendar) and present in class
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork as learners discuss the major migration events
Creativity and imagination: networking as learners sing a Qasida of welcoming the Prophet
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — movement of people
scopeNotes: include: the named sequence of migration events (leaving Ali in his house → departure with Abubakar → cave Thaur → incident of Suraqah → reception in Madina) is an explicit, curriculum-stated ordered list — a legitimate 'ordering' branch content source, not an invented sequence.

subStrands.name: 7.4 Constitution of Madina
subStrands.notes: Numbered '7.4' in the Summary of Strands and Sub-Strands table but '7.5' in the detailed strand body text (with no 7.4 heading appearing in the detail section at all) — an apparent numbering inconsistency in the source PDF, recorded verbatim per mining discipline rather than silently resolved.
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the terms of Madina constitution
assess the importance of Madina constitution to the history of Islam
describe the role played by the Ansar in the settlement of Muhajirun in Madina
develop a desire to maintain Islamic brotherhood as per the teachings of Islam
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Madina constitution important to history of Islam?
What role did the Ansar play in the settlement of the Muhajirun?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the terms of Madina constitution, and present on a manilla paper
discuss the importance of Madina constitution to the people of Madina and in the history of Islam
listen/watch a story on how united the Muhajirun and the Ansar were
discuss the role played by the Ansar in settling the Muhajirun (such as shared their wealth, assisted them in integration and settlement), and write notes
discuss the lessons learnt from the spirit of brotherhood established by the Prophet (S.A.W) (Muslims must be united, assist one another)
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork discussing the importance of Madina constitution
Learning to learn: sharing learnt knowledge as learners discuss the lessons learnt from the spirit of brotherhood
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — social cohesion and constitution making
scopeNotes: include: the Ansar's role is named specifically (shared their wealth, assisted in integration and settlement) — not just 'welcomed the Muhajirun' in general terms.
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Strand-level (7.0 History of Islam) rubric top band requires narrating events AND comprehensively applying lessons from Islamic historical events in life — bare narration without an applied-lesson dimension is only mid-band.
